selected.where: Early return for len(lst) == 1 returns lst[0] without applying index-based power rules.
selected.how: The singleton shortcut bypasses the specification requiring squaring for index 0 (multiple of 3).
selected.what: Input [2] returns 2 instead of 4; input [-2] returns -2 instead of 4.

selected.where: Early return for len(lst) == 2 returns sum of elements without applying index-based power rules.
selected.how: The two-element shortcut bypasses the specification requiring squaring for index 0.
selected.what: Input [2, 3] returns 5 instead of 7 (4+3); input [-2, 3] returns 1 instead of 7.

selected.where: Condition (i % 4 == 0) and (i % 3 != 0) inside an elif following i % 3 == 0.
selected.how: The elif is unreachable for indices divisible by 4 because the prior if catches multiples of 3 first.
selected.what: Index 4 (multiple of 4, not 3) is squared instead of cubed; e.g., [0,0,0,0,2] sums to 4 instead of 8.
